findings.issue_text: `updateManyByCredentialId(..., {})` does not update Prisma `@updatedAt` fields when the data object is empty, so the calendar-refresh timestamp is never updated.
The migration's `DEFAULT NOW()` backfill assigns the migration time to every existing cache row, causing the “Last updated” UI to report deployment time rather than the actual cache population time.
Webhook-test initialization failures call `cleanup`, which always exits `0`, so automation treats failed webhook setup as successful.

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration's `DEFAULT NOW()` backfill assigns the migration time to every existing cache row, causing the “Last updated” UI to report deployment time rather than the actual cache population time.

adjudication.rationale: The migration in `20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql` adds `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()`, which means all existing CalendarCache rows will get the migration timestamp as their updatedAt value. This is technically correct behavior for a migration adding a new required column, but the finding correctly identifies that this will show misleading 'Last updated' times in the UI for pre-existing cache entries. However, this is not a bug per se - it's a known tradeoff when adding timestamp columns to existing data. The schema also has `@updatedAt` which will correctly update the timestamp on future modifications. This is more of a data accuracy concern for historical data rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook-test initialization failures call `cleanup`, which always exits `0`, so automation treats failed webhook setup as successful.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the script test-gcal-webhooks.sh, the cleanup function always calls 'exit 0' regardless of why it was called. When the rate limit is hit (line 47-50), the script calls cleanup() which exits with code 0, making it appear successful. Similarly, when URL extraction fails (line 55-57), cleanup() is called and exits 0. This means automation or CI systems would incorrectly treat these failure scenarios as successful runs. The cleanup function should either accept an exit code parameter or the error paths should exit with non-zero codes before calling cleanup.
